result.description: Open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin for running online stores; core REST API exposes store data (products, orders, customers, etc.).
result.auth_detail: Per-store consumer key/secret (generated in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API, or via /wc-auth/v1/authorize flow) used as HTTP Basic over HTTPS, or OAuth 1.0a one-legged signing over HTTP. WordPress Application Passwords used for MCP. No central OAuth2 app registry; each store is separate (self-hosted).
result.access_detail: Core plugin is free; any store owner/admin generates keys self-serve. No vendor app review. Credentials are per-store, so end users must supply store URL + keys (or use /wc-auth/v1/authorize flow).
result.api_notes: WP-integrated REST API v3 with full CRUD in JSON across products, orders, customers, coupons, refunds, shipping, taxes, settings, reports, webhooks, etc. Requires WooCommerce 3.5+, WordPress 4.4+, pretty permalinks. Store-hosted base URL varies per site.

evidence.quote: WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API.
You must use OAuth 1.0a "one-legged" authentication to ensure REST API credentials cannot be intercepted by an attacker.
This documentation is about the free, core WooCommerce plugin
These two keys are your Consumer Key and Consumer Secret.
WooCommerce (WC) 2.6+ is fully integrated with the WordPress REST API.
The current WP REST API integration version is v3 which takes a first-order position in endpoints.
The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview.
Remote HTTP connections authenticate using a WordPress username and an Application Password.
